fit: olive oil exposure and Parkinson anxiety severity
assessment: Olive oil is one item in a Mediterranean diet-adherence questionnaire; no isolated oil or Parkinson anxiety contrast.

fit: coffee exposure and Parkinson fatigue severity
assessment: The introduction cites roasted coffee as a source of some thiazole compounds. The original uses other test compounds and does not assess coffee or a Parkinson outcome.

fit: cranberry exposure and Parkinson depressive symptom severity
assessment: Editorial cites an oral gel containing cranberry alongside other botanicals in laboratory work, not a depression comparison.

fit: cod exposure and Parkinson fatigue severity
assessment: Review describes cod peptide-derived hydrogel as experimental material; this is not grilled fish or a fatigue comparison.

fit: coffee exposure and Parkinson fatigue severity
assessment: Coffee appears among activities in dementia care guidance. The report gives no isolated coffee comparison or Parkinson symptom measurement.

fit: ginger exposure and Parkinson anxiety severity
assessment: The review mentions ginger-derived particles as related preclinical context. It does not test a culinary ginger preparation or the assigned clinical outcome.

fit: mango exposure and Parkinson depressive symptom severity
assessment: Rat neurotoxicity study tests isolated mangiferin and identifies mango as a source; no culinary mango Parkinson outcome.

fit: fennel extract drops and pooled premenstrual fatigue domain
assessment: The emotional domain includes fatigue and reduced energy. Three-group p=.29 and the means do not identify a fatigue-only outcome. The extract does not verify toasted seed.

fit: shiitake mechanically identified in symptomatic esophageal impaction
assessment: Endoscopy confirmed shiitake after mealtime dysphagia. Preparation is unknown and the lower-esophageal obstruction is distinct from a Parkinson swallowing comparison.

fit: reported transient swallowing symptoms after shiitake with probable esophageal disease
assessment: Transient food stopping, choking and discomfort were reported. Suspected eosinophilic esophagitis and unknown meal preparation limit transfer. The fresh skin-test material is not the exposure history.

fit: shiitake airway obstruction during custard meal in multiple sclerosis
assessment: A complete meeting member identifies shiitake as the obstructing object. Pre-existing cough with liquids and unknown mushroom preparation limit inference about Parkinson swallowing severity.

fit: oven-treated shiitake and controlled food texture measurements
assessment: The original table shows generally lower hardness and more absolute adhesiveness after longer oven treatment. Instrument readings cannot establish a swallowing symptom direction.

fit: Parkinson manometry with varying bolus viscosity, no mushroom exposure
assessment: Instrumented volume and viscosity comparisons measure physiology in PD. The authors did not test solid consistency in that protocol. No roasted shiitake effect estimate is available.

fit: shiitake powder exposure and non-specific gastrointestinal adverse symptoms
assessment: Two participants reported gastrointestinal symptoms with eosinophilia. The inspected original abstract does not identify a swallowing outcome or roasted exposure.
